page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by a 12-core, 24-thread Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The instance features 192.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local disk storage or bundled GPUs, relying on network-attached storage with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Single-threaded execution demonstrates weaker baseline performance highlights, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0 and a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1108.98. Multi-core performance reaches average operational tiers, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 18392.83 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7163.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks reflect average performance, recording 96.89 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 52.55 GB/sec for write operations.

The hardware configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency by providing substantial RAM density relative to core count without attached GPU overhead. Tradeoffs favor concurrent multi-threaded processing and capacity-heavy memory usage over single-core speed. Demonstrating 16.8 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, this configuration fits in-memory caching, relational databases, static web serving, and memory-intensive backend applications.

Equipped with 192.0 GB of system RAM, it provides an 8.0 GB memory allocation per vCPU. The server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate lower single-threaded throughput, reflected in a 935.0 Geekbench single-core score, alongside moderate multi-core scalability reaching a PassMark CPU score of 18392.83. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth reach 96.89 GB/sec and 52.55 GB/sec, respectively. Supported by instruction extensions including AVX-512F and AES, this instance offers efficient resource allocation for memory-heavy enterprise tasks such as Redis in-memory caches, relational database systems, and static web serving.
